title: Price objection — website quote 'higher than expected'
summary: A yoga studio owner pushes back on your quote. Keep the price and the relationship.

brief.counterpart: Sofia, owner of a yoga studio
brief.your_goal: Keep the price (or trade scope), keep the relationship, agree a next step
brief.setting: You sent a quote of $4,800 for a 10-page site with class-booking integration. Sofia asked for a follow-up call.

persona.name: Sofia
persona.mood_at_start: Warm but anxious about money; apologetic when pushing back.
public_facts: Runs a studio with about 25 classes a week
Current site is outdated and hard to use on mobile
Received a quote of $4,800 for a 10-page site with booking integration
persona.budget_real: Could pay the full $4,800 if it is spread over 3–4 months

variants.context: The user sent a quote of $4,800 for a 10-page site with booking integration. This is the follow-up call.
variants.user_objective: Keep the price (or trade scope), keep the relationship, and agree on the next step
variants.ai_objective: Get the price down without seeming rude

hidden_facts.fact: Budget is not fixed: Sofia could pay the full amount if it were spread over time.

unlock.behavior: user explores payment terms or asks what would make it work

black_swan.fact: Her real concern is not price but whether she can update the class schedule herself; her previous site needed a developer for every change.

unlock.behavior: a label about her worry or a calibrated question about what matters most to her

objections.text: It's more than I expected, honestly.
objections.trigger: early in the call, after the quote is mentioned

objections.text: My friend's site cost about half that.
objections.trigger: the user defends the price with features or effort

success_criteria: Deal at full price, with scope traded, or with a payment plan
failure_conditions: Discounted within 2 turns of the objection
